issue.title: Update for new versions of SQLAlchemy
issue.body:
SQLAlchemy 1.4 made some changes that are currently incompatible with this extension. Identify failing tests and make changes to fix those. We should also pin to `SQLAlchemy<2`, since that will be a bigger change and will be more appropriate in Flask-SQLAlchemy 3.0.

Here's some that I'm aware of so far:

- [x] #885 `URL` is immutable

body: I would see if Flask can remove this meaningless joinedload() as it is not necessary here.

OK this is extremely specific to just the query.count() method.    Usually, options that make no sense raise an error, including on 1.3, such as:

    s.query(A.id).options(joinedload(A.bs)).all()

I'll adjust query.count() to behave as closely to the old way as possible as this is all frozen in time stuff.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Move enable_eagerloads(False) out of _from_self() into count()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2633

As always, thanks a lot @zzzeek. I confirm the fix works.

> I would see if Flask can remove this meaningless joinedload() as it is not necessary here.

I tried to keep the example as minimal as possible. The `joinedload()` is necessary for me, because the relationship is defined with `lazy='raise'` and I use the same query to `count()` the number of items, and access the relatated object.

> As always, thanks a lot @zzzeek. I confirm the fix works.
> 
> > I would see if Flask can remove this meaningless joinedload() as it is not necessary here.
> 
> I tried to keep the example as minimal as possible. The `joinedload()` is necessary for me, because the relationship is defined with `lazy='raise'` and I use the same query to `count()` the number of items, and access the relatated object.

that sounds very strange, query.count() does not access any related object, can you please clarify what you're doing there?    note that Query is legacy overall, so the whole pattern here is no longer the "best" way to do it.

What I'm doing is:

```python
query = session.query(User).options(joinedload(User.parent))

count = query.count()
items = query.items()
```

or, with flask-sqlalchemy:

```python
def my_endpoint():
  query = query.options(joinedload(User.parent))
  res = query.paginate(page=0, per_page=30)
  schema = schemas.UserListSchema()
  return schema.dump({'data': res.items, 'meta': res})
```

(I can provide full working examples if necessary)


What is the "best" way to achieve this?

you would have two separate queries:

```python
count = session.query(func.count()).select_from(User).scalar()

items = sesion.query(User).options(joinedload(User.parent)).all()

```

the idea is that this does not rely on implicit guessing and you also get a much more efficient query for the COUNT part, as the ORM's .count() method has to run everything in an inefficient subquery.

issue.title: Any load options break `with_entities()` in 1.4

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: with_entities change
labels.description: issues related to the altered behvaior of Query w/ 1.4/2.0

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Very similar to #6052 (which is supposedly fixed?), applying any loader option breaks `with_entities()`.

**Expected behavior**
No error, this output from the test script:

```
normal
[<Thing 1>]
with entities + noload
[(1,)]
with entities + joinedload
[(1,)]
```

**To Reproduce**

```py
from sqlalchemy import *
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base  # to test on 1.3
from sqlalchemy.orm import *


Base = declarative_base()


class Thing(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'things'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    owner_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=True, index=True)
    owner = relationship('User', backref='things')

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Thing {self.id}>'


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'users'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.id}>'


e = create_engine('postgresql:///test', echo=False)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)
s = Session(e)

if not s.query(Thing).count():
    thing = Thing(owner=User())
    s.add(thing)
    s.commit()


print('normal')
print(s.query(Thing).all())
print('with entities + noload')  # fails
print(s.query(Thing).options(noload('owner')).with_entities(Thing.id).all())
print('with entities + joinedload')  # fails
print(s.query(Thing).options(joinedload('owner')).with_entities(Thing.id).all())
```
